name: Stellmark Concord Overcoat
description:
A long, structured overcoat in charcoal, navy, or camel — the kind that says you have somewhere to be and it matters. The Stellmark Concord is cut from a wool-polyester blend that drapes well and resists wrinkling even after a full day in a pressurized transit pod. The lapels are moderate, the buttons are real horn, and the silhouette is classic double-breasted with a subtle waist suppression. Nothing about it is loud. Everything about it is intentional.

Stellmark is a Tier 4 clothier that occupies the space between bespoke tailoring and corporate retail — expensive enough to signal success, accessible enough that mid-level executives can justify it on an expense account. The Concord is their anchor product. It's the coat a Tier 3 professional buys when they get promoted and a Tier 4 executive replaces every three years without thinking about it.
what_it_says: You've arrived, or you're very convincingly pretending to have arrived.
story_hooks: Two executives at a merger negotiation are wearing identical Stellmark Concords — one of them is not who they claim to be.
A Stellmark tailor has been quietly altering coats for clients who want hidden document pockets — and has been keeping copies of everything passed through them.
A Tier 2 knockoff of the Concord is being sold in the working-class markets; it's nearly identical, and someone at Stellmark is furious enough to hire investigators.

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding silhouette that commands respect without demanding attention. Long, structured overcoat that hits mid-thigh, with clean architectural lines and deliberate proportions. Classic double-breasted front with moderate lapels that frame the torso with precision. The coat moves with understated authority—drapes rather than clings, settles rather than hugs.
physical_description.fit: Tailored with subtle waist suppression that suggests the wearer's form without clinging. Relaxed through the shoulders but structured at the chest. Sleeves taper slightly toward the wrist. Built for layering over corporate workwear or street augmentation harnesses alike.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-polyester blend (likely 65/35 or 60/40 ratio) engineered for wrinkle resistance and durability in pressurized transit environments. The weave is dense enough to hold shape after 14-hour shifts in climate-controlled corporate towers or heated subway pods.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost liquid drape with a subtle nap that catches light differently depending on angle. The wool brings warmth and slight texture; the polyester ensures sharp creases and minimal maintenance. Feels structured but not stiff—institutional quality elevated to executive standard.
physical_description.color_scheme: Offered in charcoal (most popular—universal, conservative, hides wear), navy (second choice—slightly warmer, signals established presence), or camel (least common—worn by Tier 4 executives confident enough to stand out). Subtle tonal variations in the weave prevent flatness.
physical_description.closures: Six real horn buttons (not synthetic) down the front in a traditional double-breasted arrangement. Horn has slight translucency and warm ivory tone. Buttons are the only luxury detail; the rest is calculated restraint.
distinctive_features: Real horn buttons (horn sources verified through GLMZ supply chains—status symbol for mid-tier)
Internal magazine pocket (corporation-standard, sized for datapads or secure documents)
Reinforced interior lining in synthetic microfiber (hides wear, resists moisture from transit pods)
Subtle Stellmark woven label at interior neck (small enough to be professional, visible enough to those who know)
Functional cuff buttons (rare in this price range—suggests tailor-adjacent construction)
No visible augmentation integration points (the coat doesn't acknowledge chrome; it exists above such concerns)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 aspirational / Tier 3 achievement. Entry-level executive wear. Signals someone who has made it past hourly wages but hasn't entered the rarefied air of Tier 1 corpo elite (who wear bespoke, often with integrated smart-fabric tech).
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by mid-career professionals navigating the boundary between blue-collar skilled work and white-collar management. Corporate middle management, mid-tier legal/medical professionals, successful independent consultants. The coat says: 'I've earned my seat at the table.' It does not say 'I own the table' or 'I'm struggling to stay at the table.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on first wearing; broken-in after 6-12 months with subtle creasing at the elbows and hem. The wearer likely dry-cleans monthly. Minor scuffing at the cuffs from transit pod armrests. After 2-3 years, it develops a soft patina—creases that settle into the weave, button holes that soften slightly, a subtle shine on the lapels from collar rubs. Still respectable at five years; rarely worn past six.

image_prompt: Fashion photograph of a Stellmark Concord Overcoat in charcoal gray on a poised cyberpunk-era model, shot against a moody backdrop of GLMZ architecture—neon-tinged brutalist corporate towers blurred in the background, cool blue and amber lighting. The model stands three-quarter angle, one hand at the coat's lapel, the other relaxed at their side. The coat's drape is the focus: sharp, architectural, uncompromising. Shot from waist-up to showcase the double-breasted silhouette and moderate lapels. Subtle augmentation visible (chrome earlace or subcutaneous glow under jawline) to ground the figure in 2226, but the coat itself is aggressively analog-elegant. Moody key lighting emphasizes the weave's subtle nap. Dark, minimal studio or urban underpass setting. Professional, aspirational, the kind of image that would appear in a Stellmark corporate lookbook or mid-tier professional wardrobe guide. --ar 2:3 --v 6
